spark.scene: Dark ocean with scattered white cumulus and cirrus across the Hawaiian Island chain, dense white cloud covering the southeastern large island and extending south, with a diffuse gray translucent veil trailing southwest over the ocean west of the large island.

plumes.visual_description: diffuse pale gray translucent veil extending southwest from the cloud-covered large island over dark ocean, smoother and less bright than surrounding white cumulus

track.note: Centroid drift of a plume still attached to its source is slower than the air; direction is the main signal, speed is approximate.

per_plume.source_hint: upwind/source end near Maui Channel ~20.1N 156.0W, ~90 km from Mauna Loa and ~118 km from Kilauea; no fire or eruption source
evidence: USGS HVO at image time reports Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW not erupting (paused summit eruption) and Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, so no active eruptive vog source. [E1]
NASA FIRMS for 2026-08-23 shows no fire clusters and no summit volcanic thermal in Hawaii box, giving no support for wildfire_smoke. [E5]

Plume centroid is 164-195 km from summits, wind-aligned upwind end still 90.6 km from Mauna Loa and 117.6 km from Kilauea, and tracked source end at 20.095N 156.045W is 82.7-110.6 km from summits, not anchored at either vent, arguing against vent-trailing vog. [E6, E7, E3]

Measured drift toward 255 deg at 9.6 km/h compares to centroid wind from 48 deg (toward ~228 deg) difference ~27 deg within 45 deg, supporting NE-to-SW transport; summit wind from 18 deg and source-end wind from 29 deg also blow toward ~198-209 deg southwest, explaining SW elongation without identifying source. [E3, E4, E8, E9]

Mask is entirely oceanic with land_frac 0.0, so faint gray translucent veil southwest over dark ocean is reliably located but its smooth pale-gray appearance distinct from bright white cumulus remains ambiguous between thin cloud/cirrus outflow and dilute haze. [E2]

NASA FIRMS for 2026-08-23 shows no fire clusters and no summit volcanic thermal in Hawaii box, giving no support for wildfire_smoke.

Plume centroid is 164-195 km from summits, wind-aligned upwind end still 90.6 km from Mauna Loa and 117.6 km from Kilauea, and tracked source end at 20.095N 156.045W is 82.7-110.6 km from summits, not anchored at either vent, arguing against vent-trailing vog.

Measured drift toward 255 deg at 9.6 km/h compares to centroid wind from 48 deg (toward ~228 deg) difference ~27 deg within 45 deg, supporting NE-to-SW transport; summit wind from 18 deg and source-end wind from 29 deg also blow toward ~198-209 deg southwest, explaining SW elongation without identifying source.

Mask is entirely oceanic with land_frac 0.0, so faint gray translucent veil southwest over dark ocean is reliably located but its smooth pale-gray appearance distinct from bright white cumulus remains ambiguous between thin cloud/cirrus outflow and dilute haze.

classify.caveats: Mostly cloudy scene with dense white cloud over SE Hawaii; faint translucent veil is morphologically ambiguous. Both volcanoes reported not erupting and no FIRMS fires, but residual degassing or thin cirrus outflow cannot be ruled out from GeoColor alone. Track fit is moderate (R2 0.51).

kilauea.activity_summary: Kīlauea volcano is not erupting; the summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. Data indicate the onset of the next fountaining episode is likely between August 24 and August 28. Overview: The summit eruption of Kīlauea in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in July, while the summit region showed patterns of slight inflation. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 57 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the July reporting period, after 94 in June. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
